title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the P.S. to a 1965 letter. The previous page closes with 'What about your θ-fns, are you going to write a book?', which suggests the recipient is Mumford, though this is not certain. Grothendieck lists the 'modular varieties' that motivic Galois theory leads one to expect. In modern language:

(1) Data. G is a connected reductive group over Q. U_R is the circle group, a one-dimensional anisotropic torus with U(R)=S^1. The map i0: U_R → G_R is a homomorphism such that:
(a) i0(-1) is central. This is the weight condition: on a representation in which i0(-1) acts as (-1)^n, one gets Hodge structures of weight n.
(b) The centralizer K_R of i0(i) has K(R)^0 maximal compact in G(R)^0. Since i0(-1) is central, Ad i0(i) is an involution, so this says Ad i0(i) is a Cartan involution of G^ad.
(c) i0 is nontrivial on every R-simple factor of G_R.

(2) Spaces. C_R = Cent(i0) ⊂ K_R. The real homogeneous variety is Q̌ = G_R/C_R. The domain 𝒱 = G(R)^0/(G(R)^0 ∩ C(R)) is the orbit of i0 under conjugation, which he calls 'Siegel-space'. In modern terms 𝒱 is a Mumford–Tate domain or flag domain, an open G(R)-orbit in the compact dual G_C/P.

(3) Complex structure and families. 𝒱 carries a G(R)-invariant complex structure. Each Q-representation V of G with a lattice V0 gives a holomorphic family of Hodge structures on 𝒱, once a weight n is fixed with i0(-1) = (-1)^n on V. The family is polarizable by choosing a G-invariant form φ.

(4) Continuation on the next page.
- 𝒱 should represent a functor on complex-analytic spaces: Tannakian, additive and multiplicative assignments of Hodge structures to all V.
- The quotients 𝒱/Γ, for Γ arithmetic, are expected to be algebraic over Q, usually over Z. He allows for possible extra conditions, either arithmetic (Frobenius elements) or geometric (G_R has no compact factor).
- A margin note says 𝒱 is in general not Riemannian symmetric. It fibres over a symmetric space with compact homogeneous projective fibres, is simply connected, and is the universal cover of 𝒱/Γ when Γ acts freely.

(5) Purpose. The aim is to describe the target of 'period maps' for motives with given motivic Galois group G. This gives a general group-theoretic moduli formalism containing Siegel and Shimura varieties.

The data are essentially Deligne's later Shimura-datum axioms (Travaux de Shimura, 1971; Variétés de Shimura, 1979), with two differences. Grothendieck uses U instead of the Deligne torus S, and he omits axiom SV1 (Ad∘h has only types (-1,1),(0,0),(1,-1)). He therefore lands on general Mumford–Tate/period domains in the sense of Griffiths and of Green–Griffiths–Kerr. He also conjectures that their arithmetic quotients are algebraic over Q.
errors: The complex structure is said to be 'inherited from one on Q̌(R)'. But Q̌ = G_R/C_R is a real variety, and its real points carry no natural complex structure. The correct source is the open embedding of the orbit G(R)/C(R) into the compact dual G_C/P, where P is the parabolic attached to the Hodge filtration. 𝒱 being 'a connected component' of Q̌(R) is also loosely stated: 𝒱 is a G(R)^0-orbit.

The conjecture that every 𝒱/Γ carries an algebraic structure over Q is false without condition SV1, i.e. when 𝒱 is not Hermitian symmetric. Carlson–Toledo and Griffiths–Robles–Toledo (2014, 'Quotients of non-classical flag domains are not algebraic') show such quotients are not algebraic. Grothendieck's hedge 'extra geometric conditions' does not name the right one: absence of compact factors is not enough, one needs the Hermitian condition.

The universal 'complex analytic family of Hodge structures' on 𝒱 ignores Griffiths transversality. Families coming from geometry satisfy transversality, so in the non-classical case 𝒱 parametrizes more than variations of Hodge structure. The margin claim of simple connectivity is fine, since the fibres are flag manifolds over a contractible base.

ideas.what: Group-theoretic data (G over Q, circle homomorphism i0 with i0(-1) central, Ad i0(i) a Cartan involution, nontrivial on simple factors) defining a moduli domain for Hodge structures with motivic Galois group G
ideas.modern_name: Shimura datum / Mumford–Tate domain data (axioms SV2, part of SV3, weight condition)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1971, 1979); Mumford (1966) for Hodge groups via the circle; Shimura for the varieties

ideas.what: Homogeneous domain G(R)/C(R) with invariant complex structure carrying tautological polarizable Hodge structures for every representation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (1968–70), Griffiths–Schmid; Green–Griffiths–Kerr for Mumford–Tate domains

ideas.what: Characterization of 𝒱 as representing a functor of Tannakian families of Hodge structures (tensor-compatible in V)
ideas.modern_name: Moduli of Hodge structures with G-structure (Tannakian description of Mumford–Tate domains)

ideas.what: Expectation that 𝒱/Γ for arithmetic Γ have models over Q (often Z), possibly under arithmetic 'Frobenius' conditions
ideas.modern_name: Canonical models of Shimura varieties; integral models
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura, Deligne, Milne, Borovoi; Kisin for integral models

ideas.what: Observation that 𝒱 is generally not symmetric but fibres over a Riemannian symmetric space with compact Kähler homogeneous fibres
ideas.modern_name: Fibration of flag domains over G(R)/K(R)

ideas.what: Polarizability follows from or accompanies the Cartan condition via a G-invariant form
ideas.modern_name: Deligne's criterion: Ad h(i) Cartan involution iff polarizable

missed.claim: In 1965 Grothendieck wrote down, as consequences of motivic Galois theory, essentially the axioms of a Shimura datum in the circle-group formulation (weight centrality, Cartan involution, nontrivial on factors). This predates Deligne's 1971 axiomatics. The standard historical account (Mumford 1966 → Deligne 1971) does not record Grothendieck's role.
missed.quote: the centralisator K_R of i_0(√-1) is such that K_R(R)^0 is maximal compact in G_R(R)^0. Moreover, for every R-simple component of G_R, the corresponding component of i_0 is not trivial.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical attribution: an early motivic-Galois-theoretic motivation for Shimura data, and for Mumford–Tate domains in general rather than only Hermitian ones.

missed.claim: He conjectured that all arithmetic quotients of such general (non-Hermitian) Mumford–Tate domains are algebraic over Q or Z. He left open what extra conditions are needed and anticipated a role for 'Frobenius elements'. The Hermitian case became Shimura varieties. The non-Hermitian case was later shown to be non-algebraic (Griffiths–Robles–Toledo), so this is an early wrong expectation.
missed.quote: The modular varieties I expect to carry algebraic structures over Q (and usually, Z) are the varieties 𝒱/Γ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It connects to current work on arithmetic aspects of non-classical Mumford–Tate domains (Carayol's work on non-classical automorphic cohomology, Green–Griffiths–Kerr) and gives a historical precedent for seeking arithmetic structure there.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clear, early (1965) group-theoretic formulation of Shimura/Mumford–Tate domain data, motivated by motivic Galois groups. It anticipates parts of Deligne's 1971 axioms, and Griffiths's general Mumford–Tate domains, in an unpublished letter. However, it lives in the Mumford/Deligne circle, where such ideas circulated, and its central algebraicity conjecture is false in the generality stated.
transcription_corrections: First line: the group is written G with a corrected subscript (looks like E overwritten by Q), i.e. G_Q.
The crossed-out word before Q̌(R) is illegible scribble; '(a connected component)' is written above it as the replacement, and 'open' is uncertain.
The domain symbol written as 𝒱 is a script letter resembling ϒ/γ in the image; the family of Hodge structures uses a distinct script V.
Margin: '(necessarily? globally polarizable - to get polarization of the family, one picks a "form of polarization" φ on V, invariant by G)' with a crossed-out word before 'globally'.
